owners: Yelp's business summary names the owners as 'Oscar and Felix G.'. Florida Sunbiz corporate record for 2BROTHERSONSRQSERVICES LLC independently names 'Oscar D. Guerrero' as registered agent, corroborating the first name. Both real vehicles (two men) are visible together in the business's own promotional photos (assets/raw/gmaps-1.jpg, gmaps-21.jpg). Used on the site as 'Oscar and Felix, the owners themselves' in the why-us section; no last names used since only 'Guerrero' for Oscar could be confirmed and Felix's surname was not independently verified.
language_signal: No Spanish-language marketing material, captions or reviews found anywhere (flyer, shirt, Facebook video title 'For 20 years give us the best' are all in English, occasionally with imperfect grammar suggesting the owners' first language may not be English but all customer-facing text is in English). Falls back to English as the default site language per FORGE-BRIEF precedent, built fully bilingual (ES/EN toggle) regardless.
location_note: Treated as a real, publicly relevant business location (contacto.mapa embed used, not omitted) rather than a mailing-only address: their own flyer explicitly says the Lido Key $15 package is 'only in our location', and Yelp independently lists photos and services tied to this same Clark Center Ave address with categories including 'self-serve car wash' and 'drive-thru service', which only make sense for a real fixed site. This satisfies the FORGE-BRIEF exception for using the address normally instead of substituting a photo.
photos_source: scripts/gmaps_photocycle.js cycled the Google Maps photo viewer for the listing (see google_maps_url above) and returned 21 photo URLs (vs only 1 from the earlier single-photo gmaps_detail.js pull). All 21 downloaded via curl with a Chrome user-agent to assets/raw/gmaps-1.jpg through gmaps-21.jpg, verified with `file` (all decoded as real JPEG or PNG, none under 15KB; gmaps-8 was actually a PNG mislabeled .jpg by the source URL and was renamed/reconverted to .jpg for consistent serving). Visually reviewed every photo one by one before use. 3 photos are the business's own promotional/marketing graphics with heavy text overlays: gmaps-1.jpg (business-card style graphic with both owners, logo, phone and email), gmaps-17.jpg (a technician's work shirt with the phone number printed on the back) and gmaps-21.jpg (the pricing flyer with all 3 package prices). These were correctly EXCLUDED from the on-site gallery per the no-text-overlay-in-gallery curation rule, but kept on disk and used as data sources (email, alternate phone, real prices, owner photo, brand color). The other 18 photos are genuine work photos (vehicles, wheels, an active hand-wash in progress, a technician detailing a headlight, and one real before/after of a travel trailer, gmaps-20.jpg) and were curated down to 1 logo-derived nav/footer icon plus 8 used across hero, about and gallery. No stock photography used anywhere.
logo_note: No standalone transparent logo file exists publicly; the brand mark only appears embedded in the two flyer-style photos. A clean square badge (assets/raw/logo.jpg) was produced by cropping the car-silhouette glyph out of assets/raw/gmaps-1.jpg (isolating it from the surrounding contact-info text via a simple color mask, since the glyph is a distinct olive green against an icy blue background) and compositing it onto a solid dark background matching the site's own palette. This is a real crop of their real logo artwork, not a generated/invented mark.
